Title: PeekPaste: Your clipboard, within reach | Product Hunt
# PeekPaste. ## Your clipboard, within reach. PeekPaste is a native clipboard manager for Mac that stays out of your way until you need it. Push your pointer against the screen edge and your clipboard slides in. Find text, code, links, images, colors and files, search inside screenshots with on-device OCR, pin and organize clips, or open the full Library when you need more. Everything stays on your Mac - no accounts, analytics, telemetry or cloud clipboard service. PeekPaste started with a simple idea: your clipboard should always be within reach. Most clipboard managers make you open another window or interrupt what you're doing. Push your pointer against the edge of the screen and PeekPaste slides in over whatever you're working on. Find the clip you need, select it, and get straight back to what you were doing. PeekPaste remembers text, code, links, images, colors and files. You can search inside screenshots using on-device OCR, preview clips with Space, pin and organize frequently used clips, filter by app or date, and open the full Library when you need to dig further back. Clipboard history can contain incredibly personal information, so everything stays on your Mac. There are no accounts, analytics, telemetry or cloud clipboard service. Built specifically for macOS, designed to stay out of your way, and ready whenever you need something back. App Store - PeekPaste on the Mac App Store. What I feel the native screenshot tool lacks is an easy way to add annotations which a tool lightshot used to offer - is this something PeekPaste does? One other interesting idea is having an iOS app that could sync with this. Several times I've copied links, text etc only to paste it to whats app to share between the devices. All the best with PeekPaste. Supporting text, links, images, files, colors and code in one clipboard history makes this much more useful than a basic copy past tool. Do you plan to release the app for Windows? This looks so cool, I've always wanted to see what I've copied, specially images since its so easy to paste them in IDE for coding these days.

Title: Better Clipboard: Smarter copy-paste for macOS. New version! | Product Hunt
# Better Clipboard. ## Smarter copy-paste for macOS. Better Clipboard: fast macOS clipboard manager with floating carousel for copy-paste history. Browse, search, pin via shortcut/menu bar. Supports text, links, images, emojis, code—built for speed. New: Translate selected text shortcut. Apple Intelligence rewrite/translate on compatible Macs (no cloud). Features: history search, link previews, inline images/code, large emojis, shortcuts, menu bar. Free: 10 entries/3 pins. Launch tags:Mac•Productivity•Menu Bar Apps. BrandhuntDrop any domain and get entire brands online footprint. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for Better Clipboard. Built Better Clipboard to supercharge my daily copy-paste flow on macOS—sticking to native UX I love. Leverages Apple Intelligence for on-device rewrite/translate, animated cards for quick scans, and keyboard magic. Here's something most people don't realize ... when you copy formatted text, macOS doesn't store one thing. It stuffs multiple versions into the pasteboard at once: plain text, HTML, RTF, sometimes more. Then every app you paste into just silently picks whichever version it wants. Google Docs grabs the HTML. Slack ignores it and takes plain text. Email clients want inline-styled HTML. That's why the "same" paste looks completely different depending on where it lands. Do you expose those different formats in the history? Being able to pick which version gets pasted would be huge for anyone who moves content between apps all day. @leonardkim That will definitely be included in the next release. Will try...I've always had issues here when I'm pasting from my laptop to my phone and vice versa.
